newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ground troops set to fly to Gulf.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ground troops set to fly to Gulf.

text.p: The first of about 3,500 ground troops being deployed to boost U.S. military forces in the Gulf were to fly out from the Fort Hood army base in central Texas on Wednesday morning, officials said.

A military spokesman said several hundred soldiers of Fort Hood's 1st Cavalry Division would leave for Kuwait in three flights on Wednesday, the first at 10 a.m. (1100 EDT) and two more in the afternoon.
The soldiers spent Tuesday night saying goodbye to their families and making last-minute equipment checks.
President Bill Clinton said on Tuesday he had ordered the deployment to keep up pressure on Iraq's president, Saddam Hussein.

The 3,500 Fort Hood troops, joined by maintenance and medical units, were to take up position in Kuwait over the next few days. Their formal mission was to provide training for Kuwaiti forces but they could be used in any new military action against Iraq.
About 1,200 ground troops were already in Kuwait before the latest Gulf crisis began and they have stayed in place. It was Iraq's invasion of Kuwait that triggered the 1991 Gulf War.

Defense Secretary William Perry, just back from a trip to the Middle East to rally support for U.S. policy in the showdown with Saddam, said Iraq had stopped firing missiles at Western planes patrolling no-fly zones in Iraq.
That, he said, raised hopes that fresh military attacks against Iraq might not be necessary.
